Applicant :- Sahib @ Sohaeb

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Swayamanand Sisodiya
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Ankur Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Swayamanand Sisodiya, learned counsel for the informant as well as Ms. Ifrah Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 0057 of 2024, under Section 376 of I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station- Ratanpuri, District - Muzaffarnagar, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

The victim has been examined during trial as PW-3 and she has completely resiled from her earlier statements and has been cross-examined by the public Sahib @ Sohaeb vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83500269/
1 prosecutor after declaring her hostile.

entities.text: Sahib @ Sohaeb vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The other witnesses i.e. PW-1 and PW-2, who have also been examined in court and have not supported the prosecution story.
There is no likelihood of conviction of the applicant in the present case.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.05.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the bail application but could not dispute the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant and the prosecution witnesses have turned hostile.

7. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785, this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant- Sahib @ Sohaeb, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
